scope: Verified vendor identity normalization and original icon preservation

resolved_findings.finding: The new SQLite/XML/JSON adapters are described as bounded but have no measurable adapter-specific limits or required malformed/oversized/filter-boundary verification. Existing project-parser limits do not constrain SQLite query work or XML external entities.
resolved_findings.resolution: Adapter limits now specify 8 MiB metadata input, 64 KiB NICNT prefix, XML depth 64 and DOCTYPE/entity rejection, READONLY SQLite without extensions, 100 ms busy timeout, 2 million VM-operation ceiling, 25,000 output rows, 2,000 instruments per collection, bounded traversal, explicit partial errors, and malformed/oversized/filter-boundary tests.

verdict: PASS: metadata limits and failure-boundary verification now resolve the specification blocker.
nonblocking_assessment: Requiring installed content within selected roots appropriately excludes uninstalled SINE catalog entries.
Narrow vendor normalization preserves unrelated publishers and versions, and heuristic identity does not expand removal ownership.
Outstanding full-host usage adapters and web enrichment remain explicitly incomplete rather than inferred from UI wording.
limitations: Specification critique only; no product implementation or runtime verification.
No product code changed and no private metadata or .qa-criteria accessed.
